metadata.title: Ruane Cunniff's Top Q2 2026 Move: Roper Technologies Inc at a 3.55% Portfolio Impact

content.text:
Insights from the Legendary Graham-and-Doddsville Investor's Latest 13F Filing
Ruane Cunniff (Trades, Portfolio) recently submitted the 13F filing for the second quarter of 2026, providing insights into his investment moves during this period. Bill Ruane and Rick Cunniff started the firm in 1969 in the belief that they could outperform the stock market by investing in great businesses selling at reasonable prices and staying with them as long as they remained attractive. By doing exhaustive primary research, ignoring fads and sticking to their principles, the firm has built an enviable track record. William Ruane was a Graham-and-Doddsville superinvestor recognized by Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio). He was a student of Benjamin Graham, and attended his class at the same time as Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio). According to the Ruane, Cunniff & Goldfarb website, "We own quality businesses run by quality people that can compound their earnings rapidly. We hold these businesses over a long horizon with the mindset of a long-term business owner. We buy them for less than what a conservative business person would pay for them. We focus on our best ideas, while avoiding excessive concentration. All along the way, we strive to make thoughtful, rational decisions based on intensive primary research. At the core of our strategy is a belief that if we pay attractive prices to own businesses that are higher-quality and faster-growing than the average S&P 500 company, then over the long term our portfolios should earn a higher return than the S&P 500 Index with less fundamental risk."
The most significant addition was Roper Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:ROP), with 674,902 shares, accounting for 3.55% of the portfolio and a total value of $228.38 million.
The second largest addition to the portfolio was Bank of America Corp (NYSE:BAC), consisting of 3,625 shares, representing approximately a total value of $206,550.
The third largest addition was Hilton Grand Vacations Inc (NYSE:HGV), with 4,189 shares, accounting for a total value of $219,380.
The most notable increase was SAP SE (NYSE:SAP), with an additional 486,637 shares, bringing the total to 1,236,546 shares. This adjustment represents a significant 64.89% increase in share count, a 1.16% impact on current portfolio, and a total value of $190.56 million.
The second largest increase was Icon PLC (NASDAQ:ICLR), with an additional 413,476 shares, bringing the total to 2,048,087. This adjustment represents a significant 25.3% increase in share count and a total value of $355.77 million.
Summary of Sold Out
While the firm added new positions and increased existing stakes, it also exited several holdings during the quarter. The complete list of sold-out positions reflects the firm's disciplined approach to trimming or eliminating positions that no longer meet their stringent criteria for quality and valuation. This strategic pruning allows Ruane Cunniff (Trades, Portfolio) to redeploy capital into higher-conviction ideas that align more closely with their long-term investment philosophy.
Reduced Elevance Health Inc (NYSE:ELV) by 408,370 shares, resulting in a -29.42% decrease in shares and a -1.98% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $369.62 during the quarter and has returned 0.05% over the past 3 months and 14.76% year-to-date.
Reduced Sunbelt Rentals Holdings Inc (NYSE:SUNB) by 1,227,098 shares, resulting in a -22.36% reduction in shares and a -1.33% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $74.83 during the quarter and has returned 7.89% over the past 3 months and -% year-to-date.
Portfolio Overview
At the second quarter of 2026, Ruane Cunniff (Trades, Portfolio)'s portfolio included 55 stocks. The top holdings included 11.09% in Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL), 8.71% in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (NYSE:TSM), 7.73% in Liberty Media Corp (NASDAQ:FWONK), 6.56% in Charles Schwab Corp (NYSE:SCHW), and 6.11% in Capital One Financial Corp (NYSE:COF).
The holdings are mainly concentrated in 7 of all the 11 industries: Communication Services, Healthcare, Financial Services, Technology, Industrials, Consumer Cyclical, and Real Estate. This sector diversification reflects the firm's commitment to building a resilient portfolio that can weather various market conditions while maintaining exposure to high-quality growth businesses across multiple economic sectors.
The new position in Roper Technologies represents a particularly notable move for the firm. Roper Technologies is a diversified technology company that designs and develops software and engineered products across various end markets, including healthcare, transportation, and energy. The company's business model aligns well with Ruane Cunniff (Trades, Portfolio)'s preference for high-quality businesses with recurring revenue streams and strong competitive moats. The significant 3.55% portfolio allocation suggests the firm sees substantial long-term value in Roper's software-focused transformation and its ability to compound earnings over time.
Investors following GuruFocus value investing principles will note that Ruane Cunniff (Trades, Portfolio)'s Q2 2026 activity demonstrates a consistent application of their stated philosophy: buying quality businesses at reasonable prices, maintaining a long-term horizon, and making concentrated bets on their best ideas while avoiding excessive risk. The firm's willingness to establish a major new position in Roper Technologies while trimming others indicates a dynamic approach to portfolio management that remains true to its foundational principles established over five decades ago.
